MMG Ltd Names New Chief Financial Officer Amid Growth Strategy

MMG Ltd, a leading Hong Kong-based company in the Metals & Mining sector, has appointed Elaine Chan as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective July 15, 2024. The appointment comes as MMG Ltd continues to advance its operational and expansion initiatives across Asia and Australia.

Chan joins MMG Ltd from the mining division of the Hong Kong conglomerate Sunfield Group, where she served as Deputy CFO for five years. She brings over two decades of experience in corporate finance, risk management, and capital markets within the resources sector. Her appointment follows the retirement of outgoing CFO Michael Tse, who held the position for eight years and will remain as a senior advisor during the transition period.

“We are delighted to welcome Elaine Chan to our executive leadership team,” said Li Wei, Chief Executive Officer of MMG Ltd, in a statement. “Her extensive expertise in capital allocation and financial strategy will be instrumental in supporting our next phase of growth, particularly as we invest in sustainable mining practices and expand our project portfolio.”

Industry observers have noted that Chan’s appointment aligns with MMG Ltd’s emphasis on disciplined capital management and transparency. “With commodity markets remaining volatile, having a CFO with Chan’s track record of cost control and financing innovation is a prudent move,” said Kelvin Ho, senior analyst at the Hong Kong Mining Council. “Her experience in cross-border financing will also be valuable as MMG looks to diversify funding sources.”

The company recently reported first-quarter revenues of US$1.2 billion, up 7% year-on-year, citing strong demand for copper and zinc. MMG Ltd operates several large-scale mines in the Asia-Pacific region and has announced plans to increase investment in exploration and decarbonization technologies over the next three years.

In her first remarks as incoming CFO, Chan said, “I am excited to join MMG Ltd at a pivotal time for both the company and the industry. I look forward to working with the leadership team to deliver value for shareholders, employees, and local communities, while advancing our sustainability agenda.”

The Hong Kong Mining Council welcomed the appointment, stating that “Chan’s leadership will reinforce MMG’s commitment to responsible stewardship and financial resilience.” Shares of MMG Ltd were unchanged in afternoon trading following the announcement.

The executive transition is expected to be completed smoothly, with no anticipated disruption to MMG Ltd’s ongoing operations or strategic initiatives.
